statement: Trapezoid $ABCD$ has $\overline{AB} \parallel \overline{CD}$, with $AB = 6$, $CD = 14$, and height $8$. Its diagonals $\overline{AC}$ and $\overline{BD}$ meet at $P$. What is the area of triangle $BPC$?

choices.misconception: I found the area of triangle $APB$, the triangle on the short base, instead of triangle $BPC$.
I thought the diagonals cut the trapezoid into four triangles of equal area, so I took $\frac{80}{4}$.
I found the area of both side triangles together, $80 - 7.2 - 39.2$, and forgot to split it between the two of them.
I found the area of triangle $CPD$, the triangle on the long base, instead of triangle $BPC$.

hints: Triangles $APB$ and $CPD$ are similar. In what ratio does $P$ split each diagonal?
$AP : PC = AB : CD = 6 : 14 = 3 : 7$, so $P$ is $\frac{3}{10}$ of the way along $\overline{AC}$ from $A$. Find the area of triangle $ABC$ first.
Triangle $ABC$ has area $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 6 \cdot 8 = 24$. Triangle $BPC$ shares the height from $B$ and has base $PC = \frac{7}{10}AC$.

solutions.reliable: Since $\overline{AB} \parallel \overline{CD}$, triangles $APB$ and $CPD$ are similar with ratio $AB : CD = 3 : 7$, so $P$ is $\frac{3}{10}$ of the height below $\overline{AB}$, that is $2.4$ below it. Triangle $ABC$ has base $AB = 6$ and height $8$, so area $24$. Triangle $APB$ has base $6$ and height $2.4$, so area $7.2$. Triangle $ABC$ is made of triangles $APB$ and $BPC$, so the area of $BPC$ is $24 - 7.2 = 16.8$.
solutions.elegant: Triangles $ABC$ and $BPC$ share the vertex $B$ and have bases $AC$ and $PC$ on the same line, so their areas are in the ratio $AC : PC = 10 : 7$. Hence the area of $BPC$ is $\frac{7}{10} \cdot 24 = 16.8$.
